Good, that confirms the reasons flow through unmodified. I now have full path:line coverage for both questions.

## NPU power/clock state

Read by `src/xdna_top/npu_power.py`, function `read_npu_power` (npu_power.py:96-137). It's explicitly a secondary, best-effort signal — XRT submission-counter deltas remain the primary NPU-activity signal (npu_power.py:3-9).

**What it reads:** the `amdxdna` staging driver's debugfs nodes under `/sys/kernel/debug/accel/<bdf>/` (npu_power.py:30, `DEBUGFS_ACCEL`), specifically:
- `dpm_level` — a line of `npuclk,hclk` MHz token pairs, with the active one bracketed like `[400,800]` (npu_power.py:32-36, read at npu_power.py:118), parsed by `parse_dpm_level` (npu_power.py:70-93).
- `powerstate` — an SMU power-state string (npu_power.py:119).

Directory resolution is in `_debugfs_dir` (npu_power.py:39-59): a specific `bdf` must match its own dir exactly (never falls back to another accel device, npu_power.py:50-55); with no `bdf`, it takes the first sorted subdir of `/sys/kernel/debug/accel` (npu_power.py:56-57). Node reads go through `_read` (npu_power.py:62-67), which never raises.

**Distinct unavailability reasons** (all returned in `result["reason"]`, `available` stays `False`, never an exception — npu_power.py:105-137):

| Reason string | Trigger | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `"debugfs_accel_absent"` | `_debugfs_dir` returned `None` — driver doesn't export the nodes (mainline/DKMS `amdxdna` doesn't, npu_power.py:13-15), debugfs not mounted, or an unprivileged `Path.is_dir()`/`iterdir()` raised `OSError` (e.g. `PermissionError` on mode-700 `/sys/kernel/debug`) | npu_power.py:114-116 |
| `"debugfs_nodes_unreadable"` | The per-device dir exists, but both `dpm_level` and `powerstate` reads returned `None` — root-only permissions (the typical unprivileged case) or the driver doesn't populate those specific files | npu_power.py:120-124 |
| `"debugfs_nodes_unparsable"` | At least one node was readable, but `dpm_level` had no `npuclk,hclk` token (parse returns `None`, npu_power.py:87-88) and `powerstate` was empty | npu_power.py:129-131 |

Note `parse_dpm_level` also distinguishes a fourth, non-error case internally: `active: None` inside a successful parse means the node read fine but no token was bracketed (npu_power.py:74-76, 84-86) — this still counts as `available: True`, just with an unset active clock.

## iGPU telemetry discovery

Different, unrelated mechanism: `src/xdna_top/discover_sysfs.py`, function `discover_sysfs` (discover_sysfs.py:8-66). Called lazily from `load_sysfs_paths` in `src/xdna_top/gauge.py:108-130`, which `@lru_cache`s the result per process (gauge.py:108) and first checks for an explicit override file `bench_dir/e0_sysfs.json` (gauge.py:117-123) before falling back to live discovery (gauge.py:125-128).

**What it probes:**
- **Busy %**: a hardcoded list of three candidate paths, `/sys/class/drm/card{0,1,2}/device/gpu_busy_percent` (discover_sysfs.py:22-26).
- **Power**: every entry under `/sys/class/hwmon/*`, checking for a `power1_input` file and a sibling `name` file (discover_sysfs.py:39-53).

**Candidate selection logic:**
- Busy path: iterates `card0`→`card1`→`card2` in that fixed order, tries to open and read each; takes the **first one that exists and reads successfully**, then breaks (discover_sysfs.py:27-36) — first-match-wins, not best-match.
- Power path: iterates hwmon dirs in filesystem order (no sorting) and reads `power1_input` plus `name`. Selection rule at discover_sysfs.py:55: `if name == "amdgpu" or not result["gpu_power_path"]`. That means an `amdgpu`-named hwmon always overwrites whatever was previously stored (even a prior `amdgpu` match — it keeps re-assigning), while a non-`amdgpu` device is only kept if no power path has been set yet. Net effect: an `amdgpu` hwmon device wins if present; otherwise the first hwmon device with a readable `power1_input` wins.
- If nothing is found, `status` stays `"CPU-only fallback"` (discover_sysfs.py:18); a busy-path match sets `status = "iGPU found"` (discover_sysfs.py:33), independent of whether a power path was ever found.

Both paths (or `None`) are consumed in `read_igpu` (gauge.py:133) and, when missing, `snapshot.py` records distinct degraded reasons `igpu_busy_path_missing` / `igpu_power_path_missing` (snapshot.py:124-126) — the analogous "why unavailable" reporting to the NPU side, but produced by a completely separate code path.

Confirmed against the source. Here's the full picture:

## Binary resolution

`RtkService.resolveBinary()` (`src/main/services/RtkService.ts:164-203`) tries, in order:

1. **Managed binary** at `<userData>/bin/rtk` (or `rtk.exe` on Windows) — `getManagedBinPath()`, `RtkService.ts:132-135`. If present, it's version-probed; if `--version` fails, resolution returns `null` (no PATH fallback in that branch).
2. **`$PATH` lookup** via `which`/`where.exe` — `RtkService.ts:179-190`.

Managed-bin wins over `$PATH` by design (comment, `RtkService.ts:36`): *"Managed-bin resolution wins over $PATH so uninstalling Dash leaves no orphan binary."* Each candidate is version-probed with `probeVersion()` (`RtkService.ts:205-213`), which runs `execFileAsync(binPath, ['--version'], { timeout: 3000 })` — a 3s cap.

The app also maintains a `~/.local/bin/rtk` symlink to the managed binary (`ensureUserBinSymlink`, `RtkService.ts:150-153, 1014-1027`) so that Claude Code's Bash-tool rewrite (`git status` → `rtk git status`) resolves correctly outside Dash's own PTY environment. And `ptyManager.ts:239-242` prepends the managed bin dir onto spawned processes' `PATH` when the cached resolution's `source === 'managed'`.

## Windows vs everywhere else

- Exe name: `process.platform === 'win32' ? 'rtk.exe' : 'rtk'` — `RtkService.ts:133`.
- PATH-search command: `where.exe` vs `which` — `RtkService.ts:180`.
- User-PATH symlink: skipped entirely on Windows (`return null`) — `RtkService.ts:146`, since "no native release exists upstream."
- **Downloadability**: `isPlatformDownloadable()` (`RtkService.ts:273-277`) returns `true` for darwin (any arch) and linux (x64/arm64), and `false` for everything else — meaning Windows always gates off download.
- `getReleaseAssetName()` (`RtkService.ts:279-290`) has no Windows mapping, so `doDownload()` throws early on Windows (`RtkService.ts:308-312`): *"No rtk release for ${process.platform}/${process.arch}. Install manually from rtk-ai.app."* → Windows users get manual-install guidance only, no download/unpack path executes.
- Shell invocation in `runShell()`: `cmd.exe /c <cmd>` vs `sh -c <cmd>` — `RtkService.ts:780-781`.
- `ptyManager.ts:231-274` (`buildDirectEnv`) branches on `isWin` for the PATH delimiter (`;` vs `:`) and adds Windows-only env vars (`APPDATA`, `SystemRoot`, `COMSPEC`, `PATHEXT`, etc.).

## Download/unpack timeouts and retries

Module-level constants, `RtkService.ts:32-34`:

```ts
const FETCH_API_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;    // GitHub API metadata/checksum fetches
const FETCH_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000;  // archive download body (wall-clock)
const TAR_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;         // tar list/extract subprocess
```
Rationale comment (`RtkService.ts:30-31`): *"Cap download phases so a hung CDN cannot leave the single-flight promise pending forever."*

- `FETCH_API_TIMEOUT_MS` (60s), via `fetchWithTimeout()` (`RtkService.ts:994-1006`, AbortController-based) guards the GitHub releases API call (`RtkService.ts:321-327`) and the checksums.txt fetch (`RtkService.ts:422-423`).
- `FETCH_BODY_TIMEOUT_MS` (300s) is a wall-clock abort timer around the whole streamed download in `fetchToFile()` (`RtkService.ts:439-468`, timer set at 440-441).
- `TAR_TIMEOUT_MS` (120s) bounds the `spawn('tar', ...)` subprocess in both `listTarball()` (`RtkService.ts:510-513`) and `runTar()` (`RtkService.ts:539-542`).
- **Retries**: `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` (`RtkService.ts:357`), looping around `fetchToFile()` → `verifyChecksum()` → `verifyArchive()` (`RtkService.ts:357-380`); on failure the partial archive is deleted and it retries immediately (no backoff), throwing after 3 failed attempts. Comment: *"GitHub's release CDN occasionally serves truncated/corrupt bytes; retry a few times before surfacing an error to the user"* (`RtkService.ts:355-356`). The GitHub API metadata and checksum-file fetches themselves are not wrapped in this retry loop.

Unpack (`extractTarball()`, `RtkService.ts:487-502`) runs `tar -xzf ... --no-same-owner`, retrying once with `--strip-components=1` if the binary isn't at archive root; entries are pre-vetted by `assertSafeArchiveMember()` (`RtkService.ts:947-981`) against symlinks/hardlinks/path-traversal, and the archive is SHA-256 checksum-verified (`verifyChecksum()`, `RtkService.ts:983-992`) with the download URL restricted to an HTTPS GitHub allowlist (`assertTrustedDownloadUrl()`, `RtkService.ts:882-901`).

Adjacent (not part of the download path, but same file): `runHookTest()`'s stdin pipe timeout is 10s (`RtkService.ts:588`), and `runShell()`'s default timeout is 15s (`RtkService.ts:777`).

`channel/enroll.sh` owns enrollment (`fde-station/channel/enroll.sh:1`, must run as root).

**Destination paths** (`channel/enroll.sh:27-29`):
- `KEYRING_DEST="/usr/share/keyrings/fde-station-archive-keyring.gpg"`
- `SOURCES_DEST="/etc/apt/sources.list.d/fde-station.sources"`
- `AUTH_DEST="/etc/apt/auth.conf.d/fde-station.conf"`

**Keyring → apt source tie-in**: the deb822 source written at `channel/enroll.sh:81-89` includes `Signed-By: $KEYRING_DEST`, pointing directly at the installed keyring path — that's the only link between the source stanza and the keyring (no separate `trusted.gpg.d` drop).

**Credential file permission**: `AUTH_DEST` is created with `install -D -m 0600 /dev/null "$AUTH_DEST"` at `channel/enroll.sh:93`, then the secret is written under `umask 077` (`channel/enroll.sh:94-97`), and re-asserted with `chmod 600 "$AUTH_DEST"` at `channel/enroll.sh:98`. So it's **0600**, deliberately restrictive-before-write (empty file created with 0600 *before* the PAT is ever written to it), and the auth line is scoped to only this repo's path prefix: `machine raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO_SLUG} ...` (`channel/enroll.sh:96`) rather than the whole `raw.githubusercontent.com` host — comment at `channel/enroll.sh:12-13` confirms that's intentional scoping, not an oversight.

Confirmed against the source. Here's the full picture, all in `src/main/services/ptyManager.ts` unless noted:

**1. Live session tracking**
- Registry: `const ptys = new Map<string, PtyRecord>();` — `ptyManager.ts:38`, keyed by session id, `PtyRecord` shape defined at `ptyManager.ts:21-36` (holds the `IPty` proc, cwd, owner `WebContents`, kind, taskId/featureId, and an optional `TerminalMirror`).
- Added via `ptys.set(...)` at `ptyManager.ts:522` (agent spawn), `:645` (shell spawn), `:906` (arbitrary command PTY).
- Removed via `ptys.delete(...)` in each spawn path's `onExit` handler (`:551`, `:665`, `:924`) and in `teardownRecord` (`:768`), which is the shared cleanup used by the kill paths; `killAll()` does `ptys.clear()` at `:814`.

**2. Resize**
- `resizePty(id, cols, rows)` at `ptyManager.ts:695-705`: resizes the mirror (`record.mirror?.resize(...)`, line 698) then `record.proc.resize(cols, rows)` at line 700, wrapped in try/catch since "EBADF can happen during transitions."
- Wired from IPC: `ipcMain.on('pty:resize', ...)` in `src/main/ipc/ptyIpc.ts:103-110`, called from the preload bridge `ptyResize` (`src/main/preload.ts:72-73`), triggered from `TerminalSessionManager.fitTerminal()` (`src/renderer/terminal/TerminalSessionManager.ts:990-1002`) which resizes the local xterm instance first, then sends the resize over IPC (skipping sends when dimensions haven't changed, to avoid redundant SIGWINCH-driven prompt redraws).

**3. Shutdown / timeout**
- Grace window: `const GRACEFUL_KILL_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000;` — `ptyManager.ts:708` (3 seconds).
- `gracefulKillProc(proc, timeoutMs = GRACEFUL_KILL_TIMEOUT_MS)` at `ptyManager.ts:727-763`: sends `SIGTERM` (line 757), starts a timer (line 748); if the process's `onExit` doesn't fire before the timer, it escalates to `SIGKILL` (line 750). Resolves as soon as either happens.
- Why: comment at `ptyManager.ts:715-718` — node-pty's plain `kill()` sends SIGHUP, which Claude Code doesn't trap, so its in-memory session tail was lost on refresh/quit; SIGTERM + wait lets it flush to the session jsonl first.
- Callers: `killPtyInternal` (`:777-782`), fire-and-forget `killPty` (`:789-791`), awaited `killPtyAwait` (`:799-801`, used before respawn to avoid a dual-writer race), `killAll` (`:808-818`, parallel kill on quit), `killByOwner` (`:825-832`, kills PTYs owned by a closed window). IPC surface: `src/main/ipc/ptyIpc.ts:116` (`pty:kill`) and `:122-125` (`pty:kill-await`).

**4. Spawn environment specifics**
Three spawn paths, each building its own env before calling `pty.spawn`:

- **Agent PTY** (`startDirectPty` / `buildDirectEnv`, `ptyManager.ts:231-340`, spawn call at `:502-509`): sets `TERM_PROGRAM: 'dash'` (246), `HOME` (247), a merged `PATH` with a Dash-managed `rtk` bin dir prepended (248, 239-242), `COLORFGBG` from the active theme (251); on non-Windows sets `TERM: 'xterm-256color'`, `COLORTERM: 'truecolor'`, `USER` (279-281); on Windows propagates `USERNAME`/`APPDATA`/`SystemRoot`/`COMSPEC` etc. (254-277); passes an auth-var allowlist (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GH_TOKEN`, proxy vars) when not syncing the full shell env (286-303); merges user-configured `claudeEnvVars` filtered against `RESERVED_ENV_KEYS` (307-311, keys defined 127-138); merges per-worktree port vars from `WorkspacePortsRuntime` (320-324); sets `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` to disable Claude Code's own scroll handling since Dash renders it (327); conditionally sets `DASH_HOOK_PORT` (335-337).

- **Shell PTY** (`startPty`, `ptyManager.ts:563-669`, spawn call at `:617-623`): shell is `powershell.exe` on Windows else `process.env.SHELL || '/bin/bash'` (583), args are `['-NoLogo']` on Windows else `['-i']` — interactive but non-login, deliberately skipping `.zprofile`/`.zlogin` since PATH is already fixed via `fixPath()` at boot (585-588); env starts as a full copy of `process.env` (591) with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`/`ELECTRON_NO_ATTACH_CONSOLE` stripped (593-594); macOS sets `TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal` to get zsh OSC 7 cwd reporting (598-600); zsh gets `ZDOTDIR` pointed at a generated config for a custom prompt (603-604, via `ptyShellConfig.ts`).

- **Command/TUI PTY** (`startCommandPty`, `ptyManager.ts:860-929`, spawn call at `:887-893`): just `{ ...process.env, ...(options.env ?? {}) }`, no special TERM handling beyond `name: 'xterm-256color'`.

All three spawn calls pass `name: 'xterm-256color'` to `pty.spawn` for the terminfo entry.
